title: ML-guided CRISPRi combinations improve isoprenol production
summary: An ensemble of machine-learning regressors recommended combinations of up to four CRISPRi guide RNAs during six design–build–test–learn cycles in engineered Pseudomonas putida. The paper reports an approximately fivefold isoprenol-titer improvement over its control for highlighted strains. It reports 347 unique arrays for the highlighted optimization and 472 unique strains overall; these are different denominators. A 2024 DOE meeting abstract describes an earlier campaign but does not quantify the later result; the journal article date is used without claiming first public disclosure. The finding is specific to this strain and laboratory workflow, not industrial fuel production.
ai_technology: Automated Recommendation Tool ensemble of machine-learning regressors
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; Joint BioEnergy Institute; Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory; Sandia National Laboratories; University of California, Berkeley

source_review.scope: Primary publisher article/PDF and institutional preprint metadata reviewed for identity, bounded outcomes, AI role, affiliations and chronology.

evidence.tested: The article reports six optimization cycles and about fivefold higher isoprenol titer versus the stated control, with distinct counts of 347 unique arrays and 472 unique strains overall.
evidence.unknown: The result is study-specific; industrial scale-up and independent replication are not established. The earlier DOE abstract establishes a related campaign, not the later quantitative result.
evidence.ai_role: The Automated Recommendation Tool, an ensemble of ML regressors, recommended guide-RNA combinations after initial genes and training data were supplied by researchers.
